title: Split one directory out into its own repository, with its history
summary: A library inside a monorepo needs to become a standalone repository. Extract it so its commits come along — not a single 'initial commit' that throws twenty months of context away.
mental_model: Extraction rewrites every commit to contain only the paths you keep, with the subdirectory becoming the new root. Commits that touched nothing else are dropped, so the result is a history of that library alone.

setup.run: git commit -q -m "sensors: add salinity and docs"

steps.title: See the history you want to keep
steps.why: Five commits, three of which touch the sensors library. A naive copy-paste into a new repository would lose all three, along with every explanation of why the code looks the way it does.

steps.title: Clone the repository before rewriting anything
steps.why: Extraction is destructive to the clone it runs in. Working on a throwaway copy means the monorepo is never at risk, which is the standard discipline for any history rewrite.
steps.expect: A full copy, with all five commits.

verify.label: the working copy for the rewrite is ready

steps.title: Rewrite it down to the subdirectory
steps.why: `--subdirectory-filter` keeps only commits touching that path and rewrites each tree so the subdirectory becomes the root. Commits that touched nothing inside it disappear entirely.
steps.expect: Three commits, and reader.py at the repository root rather than under libs/sensors.

verify.label: nothing from the rest of the monorepo came along

steps.title: Verify the history is genuinely useful
steps.why: Each commit still explains one change to the library, and `git log -p` reads as a coherent story. That is the whole reason to extract rather than copy.
steps.expect: The original messages and diffs, now scoped to this library alone.

steps.title: Clean up the rewrite's leftovers
steps.why: Same as any filter-branch: delete `refs/original`, expire the reflog, and gc. Until you do, the extracted repository still contains every object from the monorepo.
commands: sh -c 'git for-each-ref --format="%(refname)" refs/original | xargs -n 1 git update-ref -d'
steps.expect: 0 — no trace of the app directory's blobs.

verify.label: the monorepo's other files are gone from the object database
verify.hint: delete refs/original, expire reflogs, then gc --prune=now

steps.title: Point it at its own home
steps.why: The extracted repository still has the monorepo as origin, which is a trap waiting to happen. Repoint it before anyone pushes.

verify.label: the standalone repository is published with its history

steps.title: Remove the directory from the monorepo
steps.why: Extraction copies; it does not move. The monorepo still has the library, so delete it there and add a pointer explaining where it went — otherwise the two diverge silently.

write.content:
# Libraries

`sensors` was extracted to its own repository, with history, in this commit.
Install it as a dependency instead of editing it here.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Extract the sensors library into its own repository"

verify.label: the monorepo no longer tracks the extracted library
the library became a standalone repository with its real history
verify.hint: clone, filter-branch --subdirectory-filter, then push to a new remote

verify.label: all of its code came across
none of the monorepo's other content came with it
the monorepo stopped tracking the extracted directory
the monorepo recorded the extraction as a normal commit

pitfalls: `git filter-repo --path libs/sensors --path-rename libs/sensors/:` is the modern equivalent and is far faster on a large repository. filter-branch is used here only because it ships with git.
Extraction copies history — the monorepo keeps its copy until you delete the directory there too. Two live copies is the worst outcome.
Without `--prune-empty`, every commit that never touched the subdirectory survives as an empty commit, and the extracted history is unreadable.
Tags and other branches need `-- --all` to be rewritten as well; without it you extract only the current branch.
Always run the rewrite in a throwaway clone. There is no undo once you have deleted refs/original and gc'd.

the backup refs to delete afterwards
git remote remove origin && git remote add origin <new>
remove it from the monorepo so the two cannot diverge
